recognition: This is the UCI Wine Quality dataset: 4,898 white and 1,599 red Portuguese Vinho Verde samples, with physicochemical measurements and sensory quality scores. I use that recognition only to identify the supplied data; the bundle provides no winery, vintage, panel, or intervention metadata.

candidates.title: Does residual sugar modify the alcohol–quality association within wine color?
candidates.question: Within red and white wines separately, is the association between alcohol and sensory quality weaker at higher residual_sugar, after accounting for the other measured chemistry?

core.object: Wine samples and their measured chemistry and quality scores
core.relation_or_action: Interaction between alcohol and residual_sugar in their conditional association with quality
core.contrast: The alcohol–quality association at lower versus higher residual_sugar within each color
core.prediction: I predict a less positive alcohol–quality association at higher residual_sugar in at least one color; a consistently null interaction would count against this balance hypothesis.
core.independent_unit: One wine sample; independence across samples cannot be verified from the supplied metadata.

candidates.failure_condition: The predicted interaction is absent or reverses across reasonable ordinal-model specifications and within-color checks.
assumptions: The score is treated as ordinal sensory quality, not a direct measure of consumer preference.
Measured covariates do not remove unmeasured confounding; observational associations will not be interpreted as intervention effects.
Rows are not assumed to represent independent producers or vintages.
candidates.required_new_data: None for an observational test. To establish an intervention effect, collect replicated, blinded sensory ratings from controlled wine lots varying alcohol and residual sugar factorially within color, with lot as the independent unit.
candidates.domain_value: Could identify whether alcohol's association with sensory scores depends on sweetness, a potentially useful constraint on fermentation or blending decisions, while making no causal recommendation from the existing data alone.
candidates.discriminating_delta: Tests a prespecified alcohol-by-sugar contrast within color rather than ranking predictors or asserting a general alcohol effect.

candidates.title: Is the quality association with sulfur dioxide tied to its free fraction?
candidates.question: Within each color, does the association between total_sulfur_dioxide and quality differ with the free_sulfur_dioxide share of total sulfur dioxide, conditional on measured chemistry?

core.object: Wine samples, sulfur dioxide measurements, and quality scores
core.relation_or_action: Modification of the total sulfur dioxide–quality association by the free fraction
core.contrast: Samples with lower versus higher free_sulfur_dioxide / total_sulfur_dioxide at comparable total sulfur dioxide
core.prediction: I predict that the total sulfur dioxide association differs by free fraction; no reproducible difference would reject this proposed distinction.
core.independent_unit: One wine sample; producer and batch clustering are unknown.

candidates.failure_condition: The interaction is absent, unstable to outlier handling, or depends on extrapolating beyond overlapping sulfur ranges.
assumptions: The ratio is a descriptive proxy, not a direct measurement of sulfur binding or sensory exposure.
Measured chemistry is insufficient for causal interpretation.
Sensory score comparability across samples is assumed but not documented.
candidates.required_new_data: None for an observational association test. Mechanistic interpretation would require direct sulfur speciation and repeated blinded sensory measurements on independent lots.
candidates.domain_value: Could distinguish whether two sulfur dioxide summaries carry different conditional associations with sensory scores, helping prioritize a direct speciation measurement.
candidates.discriminating_delta: Focuses on a chemically interpretable contrast between free and total sulfur measurements, not generic feature importance.

candidates.title: Do red and white wines differ in score at comparable measured chemistry?
candidates.question: Among red and white samples with overlapping physicochemical profiles, is there a residual color-associated difference in the distribution of quality scores after matching or adjustment on measured chemistry?

core.object: Red and white wine samples in the shared chemistry region
core.relation_or_action: Association of color with quality conditional on measured chemistry
core.contrast: Quality-score distributions for red versus white samples with comparable measured profiles
core.prediction: I predict a residual difference in score distributions; no difference in the common-support region would weaken this hypothesis.
core.independent_unit: One wine sample, with producer, vintage, and panel dependence unobserved.

candidates.failure_condition: There is insufficient covariate overlap, or the apparent difference disappears under common-support matching and reasonable adjustment choices.
assumptions: Color is not randomized and can proxy for unmeasured production and panel differences.
The score distributions are comparable across the two subsets, which the bundle does not establish.
Only conclusions about conditional association are warranted.
candidates.required_new_data: None for an adjusted observational comparison. To separate color perception from production and panel effects, use blinded, randomized evaluations of matched wines by the same panel, with wine lot as the independent unit.
candidates.domain_value: Could show whether one chemistry-to-score relationship can be pooled across color types or requires separate calibration, subject to the dataset's missing provenance.
candidates.discriminating_delta: Targets a conditional red–white score contrast on shared chemistry support rather than a generic color classifier.

selection_reason: All candidates pass the stated self-assessed gates and have no history match. I1 wins the broker ordering because it is first among candidates tied on history relation and current-data feasibility. Before any computation, my forecast is that the alcohol–quality association will be less positive at higher residual_sugar in at least one color; this is a hypothesis, not a result.

task.deliverable: Within-color ordinal analysis of the alcohol-by-residual_sugar association with quality, including common-support checks, uncertainty, sensitivity to influential observations, and a clear distinction between association and causation.
task.acceptance: Report the estimated interaction and uncertainty separately by color, state the independent-unit limitation, assess whether the comparison has adequate overlap, and classify the result as support, failure, or inconclusive without converting observational findings into intervention claims.
